contents.name: Organization
contents.description: A parent class that represents either the sponsor or the institution with a wargame department in the wargame design process.

contents.name: Person
contents.description: A parent class that generalizes all participants in a wargame design process.

contents.name: Sponsor
contents.description: The person or organization that contacts a wargame department with the expectation that a wargame can address their problem.

contents.name: Sponsor Org
contents.description: Characterize the sponsor as a organization that contacts a wargame department to address a problem.

contents.name: Sponsor Person
contents.description: Characterize the sponsor as a person who contacts a wargame department to address a problem.

contents.name: Wargame Team Member
contents.description: A member of the wargame team assigned to conduct the wargame design process to address a sponsor's problem.

contents.name: Wargame Team
contents.description: A group within the wargame department assigned to conduct the wargame design process to address a sponsor's problem.

contents.name: Game Director
contents.description: The wargame team member responsible for coordinating the wargame design team, controlling the game clock and its pace, ensuring that the scenario presents challenges to the players, and coordinating the post-game analysis.

contents.name: Umpire
contents.description: The wargame team member responsible for adjudicating players' decisions based on their experience and the rules, determining the outcomes of the engagements and actions.

contents.name: Analyst
contents.description: The wargame team member responsible for assessing the players' decisions and analyze the reasoning, ideas, insights, and discussions behind those decisions.

contents.name: Controller
contents.description: The wargame team member responsible for monitoring players' actions and can hide or modify information, inducing delays and challenges for players, and keeping the game on schedule.

contents.name: Game Designer
contents.description: The wargame team member responsible for defining wargame characteristics, objectives and rules, developing the scenario, balancing forces, scope, and pace, and determining the decisions players are expected to make to achieve objectives, as well as the game mechanics that translate these decisions into actions.

contents.name: Wargame Department
contents.description: The department of an organization that has the knowledge and capability to design a wargame to address a problem.

contents.name: Problem
contents.description: A complex issue that motivates the sponsor to contact a wargame department for resolution.

contents.name: Problem Assessment
contents.description: A material relationship in which the wargame department assesses whether a wargame can address the sponsor's problem.

contents.name: Schedule
contents.description: A structured timeline that outlines the sequence of events, phases, and time allocations for the wargame's execution, including preparation, gameplay, and post-game analysis.

contents.name: Preliminary
contents.description: The draft of the schedule that may require refinement.

contents.name: Established
contents.description: The schedule approved by the game director and shared with the wargame team.

contents.name: Scope Meeting
contents.description: The meeting where the game director and the sponsor approve the scope of the wargame.

contents.name: Assumption Validation
contents.description: An activity within the scope meeting to confirm the assumptions proposed for the wargame design.

contents.name: Scope Planning
contents.description: An activity that outlines the purpose, objectives, assumptions, and limitations, necessary to design and execute the wargame effectively.

contents.name: Model
contents.description: A corresponding abstraction representation of a system, entity, phenomenon, or process supporting the assumption proposed for the wargame design.

contents.name: Data
contents.description: A corresponding data supporting the assumption proposed for the wargame design.

contents.name: Assumption
contents.description: A predefined condition about the scenario, setting, rule or unit that is taken as valid to simplify the game design and execution.

contents.name: Literature Review
contents.description: An extensive research in the literature that the wargame team conduct to aid defining the scope and design of the wargame.

contents.name: Scope
contents.description: Outline what the wargame will cover, including its objectives, scenario constraints, key elements, and the decision level.

contents.name: Game Duration
contents.description: An estimated game duration predefined by the sponsor or wargame team during the scope meeting.

contents.name: Aim
contents.description: Define the primary goal or purpose the wargame seeks to achieve.

contents.name: Objective
contents.description: A clearly defined and attainable goal aligned with the wargame's aim, guiding teams' actions and decisions.

contents.name: Research Question
contents.description: Specific question that determine the key issues the wargame should address, shaping its objectives, scenarios, and evaluation criteria.

contents.name: Limitation
contents.description: Restriction related to factors such as time, resources, available data, or technological capabilities, that must be considered when defining the scope of the wargame.

contents.name: Constraint
contents.description: An specific condition or requirement that defines boundaries for the wargame, influencing its design and execution.

contents.name: Product
contents.description: Any output or deliverable generated during the wargame design process, including documents, reports, datasets, etc.

contents.name: Scenario
contents.description: The political, military, and economic background that have led to a current crisis or conflict situation.

contents.name: Setting
contents.description: The physical terrain, boundaries, and relevant environmental conditions that influence the scenario.

contents.name: Rule
contents.description: A set of guidelines dictating the game's structure, including player actions, interactions, and outcomes.

contents.name: Unit
contents.description: A military organization structured to perform specific actions within a force.

contents.name: Constraint Scenario
contents.description: A constraint that affects the crafting of the scenario in a wargame design.

contents.name: Constraint Setting
contents.description: A constraint that affects the development of the setting in a wargame design.

contents.name: Constraint Rule
contents.description: A constraint that affects the definition of rules in a wargame design.

contents.name: Constraint Unit
contents.description: A constraint that affects the definition of units employed and their actions in a wargame design.

contents.name: Analysis
contents.description: An examination of data collected from a wargame, linking player actions to objectives to identify findings, lessons, and insights.

contents.name: Database
contents.description: The database provides qualitative information on the scenario, including the physical environment and the weather conditions. It also contains quantitative information, such as the composition and arrangement of the friendly and enemy forces, logistic capabilities, weapons, and sensors. In addition, it may include rules, combat models, and their likely outcomes.

contents.name: Player
contents.description: A participant representing either a friendly or enemy force, encouraged to make independent decisions.

contents.name: Wargame
contents.description: A scenario-based warfare model involving people making decisions in a synthetic environment of competition or conflict, in which they see the effects of their decisions on that environment and then get to react to those changes.

contents.name: Specification
contents.description: The initial phase of the wargame design process when a sponsor contacts the wargame department to explain a research problem. If the wargame department accepts the sponsor's request, the sponsor and the wargame design team define the scope, objectives and contraints of the wargame design and the process advances to the design phase.

contents.name: Design
contents.description: The wargame design phase in which the game director establishes the purpose and objectives and defines key characteristics, including the decision level, format, number of sides, adjudication process, and information flow. Game designers also define the scenario, setting, rules, and combat units for each side

contents.name: Development
contents.description: The wargame design phase in which the game developers implement the wargame artifact based on the wargame design and ensure its playability and ability to achieve game objectives.

contents.name: Testing
contents.description: The wargame design phase in which the game designers and subject matter experts play a simplified version of the wargame to assess whether the game mechanics, available information, and time provided allow players to achieve the game objectives. Umpires can test and practice adjudication procedures, while game designers assess the test results and sharpen the wargame design

contents.name: Planning
contents.description: The wargame design phase in which players develop a plan based on a specific doctrine or a set of rules for analytical purposes.

contents.name: Execution
contents.description: The wargame design phase in which players either test a plan to generate knowledge for analytical purposes or make decisions to achieve game objectives for educational purposes.

contents.name: Analysis Phase
contents.description: The wargame design phase in which the analysts assess the data collected from a wargame, linking player actions to objectives to identify findings, lessons, and insights.

contents.name: Refinement
contents.description: The wargame design phase in which the game designers improve the wargame design incorporating lessons learned from the analysis phase.

contents.name: Wargame Design Process
contents.description: The main process of wargame design, which is structurally decomposed into phases, each defined as a time-based event.

contents.name: Decision Level
contents.description: Level of warfare that wargame attains according to the player's command position, the expected actions, and overarching objectives.

contents.name: Wargame Design
contents.description: The design of a wargame, including its characteristics, elements, and their relationships, crafted to fulfill learning objectives that support decision-making or serve an analytical purpose.

contents.name: Format
contents.description: The format for conducting a wargame.

contents.name: Adjudication
contents.description: The process of evaluating player decisions and interactions to determine outcomes, usually conduct by umpires, rules, or both.

contents.name: Information Limit
contents.description: The kind of information available to a player in a wargame.

contents.name: Time Progression
contents.description: The flow of time in a wargame.

contents.name: Matrix
contents.description: A more structured variation of a seminar wargame, which also focuses on players discussing their decisions, but may include an element of chance to evaluate scenarios with limited information.

contents.name: Free
contents.description: A free wargame relies on umpires' experience to determine combat outcomes. Umpires examine past engagements, missions, and campaigns to minimize subjectivity in their judgments

contents.name: System
contents.description: A system wargame uses rules and procedures to replace discussions about the outcome of players' decisions and relies on mathematical methods, typically based on probabilities, and often use a computational system to calculate them.

contents.name: Semi-Rigid
contents.description: A semi-rigid wargame uses a hybrid approach in which umpires use their experience and some \hlyellow{rules} to make their evaluations.

contents.name: Rigid
contents.description: A rigid wargame uses a set of rules, including combat results tables, to produce situations governed by the player's decisions. Adjudication proceeds strictly according to the movement, detection, and combat rules, so this game can be played with or without umpires.

contents.name: Open
contents.description: An open wargame gives players complete and accurate situational awareness. Players know information about opposing units and their positions, except for their plans.

contents.name: Closed
contents.description: A closed wargame restricts the information available to players, reflecting the real-world limitation of observing the entire battlefield.

contents.name: Strategic
contents.description: A strategic wargame focuses on national wars, often covering the entire territories of the combatants. Forces include all military units, while the time spans from years to decades.

contents.name: Operational
contents.description: An operational wargame simulate large operations and campaigns that span entire regions, periods of days to months, and involve all forces within or capable of affecting the region.

contents.name: Tactical
contents.description: A tactical wargame focuses on battles and firefights, typically set in small battle spaces with short time frames.

contents.name: Running Time
contents.description: A wargame in which time progresses continuously without interruption.

contents.name: Turn-Based
contents.description: A wargame in which time progresses discretely in turns.

contents.name: Purpose
contents.description: The overarching reason for designing the wargame.

contents.name: Cooperation
contents.description: Determines whether players or teams collaborate to achieve objectives in a wargame.

contents.name: Instrumenting
contents.description: Tools that display locations, movements, and interactions of the forces and to track data in wargames, including maps, boards, tokens, tables, charts, dice, tracking sheets, projectors, computers, software, etc.

contents.name: Educational
contents.description: An educational wargame focuses on analyzing players' decisions and understanding how and why players made those decisions, reinforcing military doctrines and other training objectives

contents.name: Analytical
contents.description: An analytical wargame aims to improve and validate a military plan or strategy to provide information for decision-making.

contents.name: Computer-assisted
contents.description: A computer-assisted wargame supports gameplay by automating combat, logistics, and record-keeping calculations

contents.name: Computerized
contents.description: A computerized wargame uses complex mathematical models to manage actions and validate players' inputs according to programmed rules. Computer aids improve visualization, recording, adjudication, and information sharing, update force positions, monitor sensor detection, and evaluate battle outcomes using combat result tables or models that factor in environmental elements.

contents.name: Manual
contents.description: A manual wargame typically relies on maps, tokens, charts, and printed materials such as rules, procedures, data, and orders of battle.

contents.name: Seminar
contents.description: A seminar wargame presents a situation to players, who discuss their actions and the most likely outcomes in an open forum.

contents.name: Deterministic
contents.description: The adjudication method in which outcomes in a wargame are determined by fixed rules and calculations without incorporating randomness or probability.

contents.name: Stochastic
contents.description: The adjudication method that incorporates randomness or probability to determine outcomes in a wargame. This can involve dice rolls, probability tables, or random number generation to simulate uncertainty and variability in combat, decision-making, or other in-game events.

contents.name: Consensual
contents.description: A consensual wargame involve the players in assessing their decisions. Players articulate and justify their actions, prompting the team to discuss the strengths and weaknesses of potential outcomes. Their ultimate goal is to reach a consensus.

contents.name: Turn Length
contents.description: Time duration of a turn in a turn-based wargame.

contents.name: Pace
contents.description: The speed of the clock time in a wargame. It typically aligns with the real-world time but can be adjusted to move slower or faster.

contents.name: Method
contents.description: Determine whether the rules in semi-rigid and rigid adjudications are stochastic or deterministic.

contents.name: Side
contents.description: A side can represent a team or a player who can make decisions that influence the gameplay.

contents.name: Cooperative
contents.description: A wargame in which players or teams cooperate by coordinating their actions toward achieving common objectives.

contents.name: Non-Cooperative
contents.description: A wargame in which opposing players or teams make decisions and take their actions toward achieving their own objectives.

contents.name: Stratetgy Payoff
contents.description: The dependence of payoffs on strategies and players in a wargame.

contents.name: Symmetric
contents.description: A wargame in which payoffs for the players depend only on the strategies, disregarding the players who use them.

contents.name: Asymmetric
contents.description: A wargame in which payoffs for the players depend on both the strategies and the players.

contents.name: Player Benefit
contents.description: The total sum of payoffs distributed among players in each adjudication.

contents.name: Non-Zero Sum
contents.description: A wargame in which the sum of payoffs for the players is always different from zero for each adjudication.

contents.name: Zero Sum
contents.description: A wargame in which the sum of payoffs for the players is always zero for each adjudication.

contents.name: Predefined
contents.description: The game designers or sponsor may predefine the wargame duration based on their experience or expectations for obtaining results, respectively.

contents.name: Undefined
contents.description: The wargame duration depends on the achievement of the objectives.

contents.name: Simultaneous
contents.description: Players or teams make decisions and choose their actions simultaneously, without a predefined turn order.

contents.name: Perfect Information
contents.description: A wargame in which all players have knowledge of the past moves of all other players.

contents.name: Imperfect Information
contents.description: A wargame in which players have limited or incomplete knowledge of the past moves of other players.

contents.name: Complete Information
contents.description: A wargame in which all players have full knowledge of the past moves, decisions, or states of other players.

contents.name: Sequential
contents.description: Players or teams take turns making decisions and choosing actions in a defined sequence.

contents.name: Player Movement
contents.description: Determine whether players or teams make decisions and choose actions sequential or simultaneous.

contents.name: Incomplete Information
contents.description: A wargame in which players have limited or incomplete knowledge of the past moves, decisions, or states of other players.

contents.name: Payoff
contents.description: The outcome assigned to a player's decisions and actions, reflecting success, failure, or progress toward objectives within the wargame.

contents.name: Learning
contents.description: Lessons players learn from their decisions, opponents' decisions, insights, and adjudication outcomes during a wargame.

contents.name: Narrative
contents.description: The story that players create through their decisions during a wargame.

contents.name: Decision
contents.description: A clear and concise statement of the action intended to be followed by the player as the one most favorable to the successful accomplishment of the assigned mission.

contents.name: Player Role
contents.description: A participant representing either a friendly or enemy force, encouraged to make independent decisions.

contents.name: Experience
contents.description: Players' own experiences that they share during a wargame.

contents.name: Sponsor Role
contents.description: The person or organization that contacts a wargame department with the expectation that a wargame can address their problem.

contents.name: Warrgame Department
contents.description: The department of an organization that has the knowledge and capability to design a wargame to address a problem.

contents.name: Problem Assessment Event
contents.description: A material relationship in which the wargame department assesses whether a wargame can address the sponsor's problem.

contents.name: Literature Review Event
contents.description: An extensive research in the literature that the wargame team conduct to aid defining the scope and design of the wargame.

contents.name: Scope Planning Event
contents.description: An activity that outlines the purpose, objectives, assumptions, and limitations, necessary to design and execute the wargame effectively.

contents.name: Assumption Validation Event
contents.description: An activity within the scope meeting to confirm the assumptions proposed for the wargame design.

contents.name: Sponsor Person Role
contents.description: Characterize the sponsor as a person who contacts a wargame department to address a problem.

contents.name: Sponsor Org Role
contents.description: Characterize the sponsor as a organization that contacts a wargame department to address a problem.

contents.name: Scope Meeting Event
contents.description: The meeting where the game director and the sponsor approve the scope of the wargame.

contents.name: Decision
contents.description: A clear and concise statement of the action intended to be followed by the player as the one most favorable to the successful accomplishment of the assigned mission.

contents.name: Player Team
contents.description: A group of players that forms a force in a wargame.

contents.name: Action
contents.description: An action undertaken by units as a result of a decision.

contents.name: Plan
contents.description: A structured strategy formulated by players or teams to achieve specific objectives within the game.

contents.name: Decision Point
contents.description: A point in space and time when the player anticipates making a key decision concerning a specific wargame.

contents.name: Information
contents.description: All available information that players are expected to use to make decisions.

contents.name: Political Factor
contents.description: Political conditions that influence the scenario and decisions, including government policies, international alliances, diplomatic negotiations, political stability, public opinion, and leadership decisions.

contents.name: Military
contents.description: Elements related to armed forces and combat operations that influence the scenario and decision-making, including force composition, troop readiness, logistical support, doctrine, command structure, and technological capabilities.

contents.name: Economic
contents.description: Resources and financial conditions that impact the scenario and decision-making, including budget constraints, resource availability, logistic sustaining, industrial capacity, economic stability, trade relations.

contents.name: Social
contents.description: Societal conditions, demographics, public opinion, and cultural dynamics that influence the scenario and decision-making, including population morale, ethnic and religious tensions, propaganda effects, civilian support or resistance, and the impact of war on social stability and cohesion.

contents.name: Information Factor
contents.description: The availability, flow, and impact of information on the scenario and decision-making, including intelligence gathering, cyber warfare, electronic warfare, media influence, misinformation, and communication ability.

contents.name: Infrastructure
contents.description: The physical and technological systems that support military and civilian operations and influence the scenario and decision-making, including transportation networks, energy supply, communication systems, water and sanitation facilities, and other essential services.

contents.name: Air
contents.description: The atmosphere, beginning at the surface, extending to the altitude where its effects upon operations become negligible

contents.name: Space
contents.description: The area above the altitude where atmospheric effects on airborne objects become negligible.

contents.name: Maritime
contents.description: The oceans, seas, bays, estuaries, islands, coastal areas, and the airspace above these, including the littorals.

contents.name: Land
contents.description: The area of the surface ending at the high water mark and overlapping with the maritime domain in the landward segment of the littorals

contents.name: Physical Terrain
contents.description: Geographical features of the battlefield that influence actions, and overall strategic decision-making.

contents.name: Time
contents.description: Temporal constraints and dynamics that influence the scenario and decision-making, including the duration of the conflict, timing of key events, deadlines for achieving objectives, seasonality, time-sensitive logistical considerations, and the speed of enemy and friendly actions.

contents.name: Cyberspace
contents.description: The global domain within the information environment consisting of the interdependent networks of information technology infrastructures and resident data, including the Internet, telecommunications networks, computer systems, and embedded processors and controllers.
